evals.prompt: Why does src/auth/session.py keep changing? Find the most contentious spots.
evals.expected_output: A ranked list of flip-flop hotspots in the file with flip counts, involved authors, and the alternating states.
expectations: The skill runs scripts/flip_flop.py against the file rather than guessing from a single git blame
The report separates genuine oscillation (flip_count > 0) from ordinary iterative edits
The report names every commit and author involved, not just the most recent change
The skill does not modify the working tree, index, commits, or branches

evals.prompt: This retry logic keeps getting reverted. Is this one person flip-flopping or a real disagreement?
evals.expected_output: A judgment grounded in flip_count, change_count, authors, and time span, not intuition.
expectations: The skill reads references/anchor-heuristics.md before making a judgment call
The skill distinguishes a single-author rapid-iteration pattern from a multi-author disagreement pattern
The skill states plainly when the evidence is ambiguous instead of overclaiming

evals.prompt: Find the most argued-over code in this whole repo before I start the refactor.
evals.expected_output: A repo-wide ranked hotspot report using the default discovery mode, with a caveat about performance bounds.
expectations: The skill uses the default hot-file discovery pass rather than walking every tracked file
The skill mentions the --max-files and --max-commits-per-file bounds if the repo is large
The skill recommends a next step (design note, decision record, conversation) rather than editing code
